I reverted the codemod's edits in `src/lib/token-usage.ts` and `src/lib/content-policy-error.ts`. Both files are now identical to before the codemod ran. `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` now passes with no errors. I didn't re-run the `build` check, but its type-declaration step failed on the same `token-usage.ts` errors, which are gone now.

**What was wrong:** the codemod meant to rewrite the AI SDK's own usage fields: `usage.reasoningTokens` became `usage.outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens`, and `usage.cachedInputTokens` became `usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens`. In these two files it also rewrote values of the repo's own `TokenUsage` type (`extracted` and `combined`). That type still has flat `reasoningTokens` and `cachedInputTokens` fields, so the new paths didn't exist.

In `token-usage.ts` it also turned `(source.outputTokenDetails as …)?.reasoningTokens` into `(…).outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens`. That reads the details object one level too deep and removes the `?.`, so it would crash whenever the details are missing.

The reads from the raw SDK usage object (`source.outputTokenDetails`, `source.inputTokenDetails`, `usage?.inputTokenDetails`) were already in the v7 nested shape before the codemod, so v6 behaviour is unchanged.

I made no other changes. No type casts or error suppressions were added, and no sites were left unfixed.
